passage: The slide line stretched past the tap. Shankar ran along the side, squeezed in between two children near the front and grabbed the ladder. "Hey!" shouted a girl. "Back of the line!" shouted the others. Shankar slid down with a big grin that faded when he looked round. Chaitanya, who had been waving Shankar over to stand with him at the back, folded his arms. At the next break Chaitanya walked past Shankar without a word, and Shankar stood by the wall alone.

qa.a: Shankar squeezed in between two children near the front of the line.

qa.q: What was Shankar feeling when his grin faded as he looked round?
qa.a: Shankar felt uneasy and a little ashamed. He got his turn, but he saw everyone was angry.

qa.q: What could Shankar have done instead, and why?
qa.a: Shankar could have gone to Chaitanya at the back and waited, or asked someone, "Can I go after you?" Shankar would get a turn and keep Chaitanya's goodwill.

qa.q: How does the pushing in look to Chaitanya?
qa.a: Chaitanya had waved Shankar over to wait together, so it feels like someone Shankar was invited to wait with chose to skip everyone. That hurts, so turning away makes sense. 😔

grounding: A child pushes to the front of the slide line, gets a turn and loses another child's goodwill.

passage: I'm Sarika, and Pranav is in my class. At recess the slide line was long. Pranav squeezed past four children and grabbed the ladder. Everyone shouted, "Pranav! No pushing!" He slid down fast. But after that, when he went to the sandpit, the others turned their backs. I don't know if he felt sorry. He played alone the rest of recess, kicking sand.

qa.q: How many children did Pranav squeeze past?
What was Sarika feeling as she watched Pranav play alone?
qa.a: Sarika was unsure and a little sorry for him, not knowing if he felt sorry.

qa.q: What else could Pranav try next time?
qa.a: Wait his turn, or ask someone, "Can I go after you?", so his friends don't turn away.

qa.q: What might recess have been like for Pranav after pushing in?
qa.a: He got a quick slide but was then shut out, so he was probably lonely and cross, kicking sand alone.

grounding: An observer describes a child who pushes to the front of the slide line, gets a quick turn, and is shut out by his friends.

passage:
Tuesday: Siami squeezed past everyone to the slide ladder. Hansa shouted, "Cheat!" Siami slid anyway.
Thursday: Siami asked Hansa to play. Hansa said, "No, you push in."
Friday: Siami stood in line behind six children. She waited, arms folded, until her turn. Then she looked at Hansa. "I waited," she said. Hansa shrugged, then smiled.

qa.q: How many children were in front of Siami on Friday?
What was Hansa feeling on Tuesday when she shouted "Cheat!"?
qa.a: Hansa was angry that Siami pushed ahead.

qa.q: What went wrong on Tuesday, and what fixed it?
qa.a: Pushing in got Siami one quick turn but cost her Hansa's trust; waiting in line on Friday started to fix it.

qa.q: How might Siami feel on Thursday when Hansa says no?
qa.a: Siami would likely feel hurt and surprised that one quick turn cost her a friend.

grounding: Over several days a child learns that pushing to the front of the line costs her a friendship, and begins waiting her turn.
